extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: XTREME-S is a benchmark for evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations across 102 languages from 10+ language families. It covers four task families—speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval—spanning 3 different domains and 7 downstream tasks. The benchmark also introduces Fleurs, a new massively multilingual speech evaluation dataset in all 102 languages.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S is assembled by aggregating multiple existing multilingual speech datasets (Fleurs, MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, Minds-14) and by collecting new recordings for the Fleurs dataset. For Fleurs, between one and three recordings per sentence were collected for 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest sets across 102 languages, with different speakers for train versus dev/test splits.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The Fleurs dataset is described as complete at more than 97%, with some missing recordings or low-quality recordings noted as potential issues to be addressed in a second version.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: FLoRes dev and devtest parallel sentences (2009 sentences in 102 languages); Multilingual LibriSpeech (derived from Librivox audiobooks); VoxPopuli (European Parliament sessions); CoVoST-2 (speech translation corpus); Minds-14 (e-banking spoken intent data in 14 language varieties).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For the Fleurs dataset, between one and three recordings were collected for each sentence (2.3 on average) across 102 languages, with speakers of the train sets being different from speakers of the dev/test sets.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Results are much better on the Western European group (11.5 average WER) than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African (26.7 average WER) or South Asian (20.7), which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages from MLS and VoxPopuli
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: FLEURS is a dataset that is complete at more than 97%; some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings); tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to e.g. speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated; test sets are not hidden to the public, so users must be careful not to inadvertently overfit on the test set
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations across speech recognition, speech classification, speech-to-text translation, and speech retrieval tasks; benchmarking multilingual speech pre-trained models; catalyzing research in universal speech representation learning; enabling data-efficient speech technology for low-resource languages
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Updates will be made on the HuggingFace platform; some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the Fleurs dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings); additional test sets may be added in the future to confirm the generalization ability of submissions
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The paper mentions several post-collection manipulation strategies encouraged for benchmark submissions: language resampling techniques for speech translation fine-tuning, TTS augmentation of training sets from MT data, back-translation or text-augmented speech model training using mC4/Wikipedia data, self-training with additional unlabeled speech, and smart filtering of unlabeled text data for domain adaptation. For the Fleurs dataset construction, between one and three recordings were collected per sentence (2.3 on average), and new train-dev-test splits were built with different speakers for train versus dev/test sets. For Minds-14, monolingual datasets were merged into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For Fleurs, 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest sets were used to build new train-dev-test splits with 1509, 150, and 350 sentences for train, dev, and test respectively, with speakers of the train sets different from speakers of the dev/test sets. For MLS, the official 10-hour splits provided by Pratap et al. were used. For VoxPopuli, only the 14 languages with more than 10 hours of data from the ASR task were used. For Minds-14, monolingual datasets were merged into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split. Scripts to download and reproduce preprocessing steps are provided.
